subject: Community Control Over Public Surveillance Ordinance
overview: The Medford City Council considered multiple resolutions and ordinances, approving both the Community Control Over Public Surveillance (CCOPS) ordinance and the Housing Stability Notification ordinance on first reading after floor amendments and public debate.

items.title: Meeting Dedication and Ceremonial Resolutions
items.summary: Dedicated the meeting to the late Chevalier Auditorium supporter Russ Rosetti and passed resolutions celebrating Black History Month and congratulating three promoted firefighters.

items.title: Approval of Records and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved prior meeting records and accepted committee reports covering planning development fees, budget process improvements, and outdoor dining regulations.

items.title: Stormwater Revolving Fund Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Approved on first reading an ordinance amendment establishing a revolving fund for stormwater management permit fees.

items.title: Roadways and Utility Repaving Resolutions
items.summary: Passed resolutions requesting DPW pothole repairs along emergency routes and requesting repaving schedules and utility restoration standards for several city streets.

items.title: Post Office Communication and Public Receptacle Requests
items.summary: Passed resolutions calling on federal officials to address local postal service delays and requesting a seasonal port-a-potty at Dugger Park and a trash barrel near St. Joseph's School.

items.title: Resolution on Budget Transparency and Reporting
items.summary: Approved an amended resolution requesting the city administration publish detailed annual budget books, board binders, and annual reports prior to FY24 budget hearings.

items.title: Community Control Over Public Surveillance Ordinance
items.summary: Approved on first reading an ordinance regulating city surveillance technology following floor amendments, public testimony, and extensive debate with the police chief. The adopted amendments include a five-year exemption for police body-worn cameras.

items.title: Housing Stability Notification Ordinance
items.summary: Passed on first reading an ordinance requiring property owners to distribute city housing rights and resource documents to tenants and foreclosed homeowners. An amendment lowering the noncompliance fine from $300 to $50 was approved, while a proposal to exempt Tufts University housing failed.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: A resident commended local letter carriers, prompting council discussion regarding postal staffing shortages.
